findings: [HIGH][DBML-CHECK][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:party_nationalities] The contract states that nationalities belong only to natural-person Parties but provides no constraint, trigger obligation, or other precise enforcement mechanism. Evidence: docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:218-226 and requirements-specification.md:BR-005/FR-003. Impact: a legal-entity Party can acquire nationality rows, violating an approved business invariant.

[HIGH][DBML-DELETION][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:parties, natural_person_details, legal_entity_details, party_nationalities, party_identifiers, party_outbox_events] Foreign-key delete restrictions protect referenced parents, but the DBML does not prohibit direct physical deletion of business, audit, identifier, nationality, or outbox rows. Evidence: requirements-specification.md:BR-020, SR-007, AC-024 and OD-004 require exclusively logical deletion and no purge; DBML references at lines 424-432 specify only relationship-level RESTRICT behavior. Impact: downstream migrations and runtime privileges cannot deterministically preserve required history and audit evidence.

[HIGH][DBML-LIFECYCLE][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:parties.record_status and party_identifiers.status] Status defaults and enums are declared, but the exact approved transitions, terminal states, immutable Party type/ownership fields, and immutable Party-Identifier value/Party/Scheme associations are neither enforced nor precisely delegated to a named mechanism with tests. Evidence: .factory/decisions.json:RG-101 and requirements-specification.md:BR-022/BR-023. Impact: persistence implementation could permit forbidden reactivation or mutation of identity-defining data.

[MEDIUM][DBML-MIGRATION][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:natural_person_details.Note, party_nationalities.Note, party_identifiers.Note] Required PostgreSQL mechanisms are not migration-deterministic. The deferred detail trigger lacks an object name, covered operations, complete timing semantics, and test obligation; the nationality partial indexes lack names and exact predicates/columns; the verified-primary partial index lacks a name and explicit migration-test obligation. The nationality note also mentions tenant columns although party_nationalities has no tenant_id. Impact: independent migration generators can produce materially different constraints or fail to implement them.

[MEDIUM][DBML-TEMPORAL][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:party_nationalities.valid_from and party_nationalities.valid_until] The declared check enforces ordering only and permits future dates, while approved BR-018, VR-009 and OD-009 prohibit future validity dates and scheduled activation or termination. No precise database or application enforcement obligation is recorded in the DBML. Impact: invalid future-dated nationality state can be persisted.

[MEDIUM][DBML-QUALITY][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:parties.display_name] display_name is declared as a denormalized value maintained atomically with a corresponding detail row, but the derivation, normalization, and behavior for each Party type are unspecified. Evidence: docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:109 and 128-134. Impact: downstream implementations must invent how to keep the denormalized value consistent.

[MEDIUM][DBML-CHECK][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:party_identifiers.normalized_value_hash] The field is fixed at CHAR(64) and described as a hexadecimal HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint, but no format constraint or precise validation obligation ensures hexadecimal content. Evidence: docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:295 and requirements-amendment-001.md:35-61. Impact: malformed fingerprints can weaken exact lookup, reconciliation, and permanent uniqueness semantics.

[MEDIUM][DBML-SYNTAX][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml] No repository-approved DBML parser or linter dependency was found, so parser acceptance could not be mechanized without prohibited installation. Bounded manual review found balanced declarations and five resolving references, but manual review is insufficient evidence for mandatory syntax acceptance. Impact: unsupported DBML syntax may remain undiscovered before migration generation.
